catalysts.name: Q3 2026 earnings
catalysts.description: Company-scheduled for Nov 2 after the close. The read is US commercial growth, sovereign-AI deals, and the FY26 guide (last raised to $8.15-8.16B).

risks: No longer clears the 20% gate (consensus ~+6%) — the catalyst trade is largely done.
~103x forward P/E: a merely in-line print can de-rate the stock sharply.
Mega-cap ($472B) — a +20% move inside a catalyst window requires a large surprise.
Government contract timing and budget politics remain lumpy.
Crowded retail/momentum ownership amplifies post-earnings swings.

macroRisk.rateOutlook: Fed funds at 3.75-4.00% after the surprise Sep 16, 2026 hike (first since 2023). The Oct 27-28 FOMC is priced ~93% hold / ~7% +25bp as of Oct 25 — but hike odds briefly spiked to ~44% after the hot Sep CPI print on Oct 14, so the path stays two-sided.
macroRisk.inflationNote: September CPI +0.6% m/m, 3.7% y/y headline; core +0.3% m/m, 2.6% y/y — both above consensus. Headline re-acceleration keeps a further 2026 hike live.
macroRisk.sectorImpact: At ~103x forward earnings, PLTR is the most valuation-sensitive mega-cap software name to real yields.
macroRisk.summary: MEDIUM — the Oct 28 FOMC is priced ~93% hold, but September CPI ran hot (3.7% headline) and a further 2026 hike is still live. October's growth/AI-infra selloff was largely a rates trade, so the decision and the dot path matter directly for this name's multiple.

catalystSpot.preRunup: PLTR typically drifts flat-to-slightly-up into earnings on elevated expectations rather than building a large pre-print run; the actual print — not positioning — drives the move. Q2 2026 saw only a modest pre-announcement pop before the real +15% move came after the beat itself.

postWin.note: 3 of the last 4 quarters produced day-of/after-hours gains (Q2 2025 +7.85%, Q4 2025 +6.85%, Q2 2026 +15%), breaking the earlier 'sell-the-news' pattern. Q2 2026 (Aug 3, 2026) was the strongest: 93% YoY revenue growth + a ~$500M FY guide raise.

postLose.note: Q1 2026 (May 4, 2026) beat on revenue but shares still fell -6.93% as the guidance raise was seen as too modest relative to sky-high expectations — the lone miss-reaction in an otherwise strong run.

spotSizing.reason: 5%. earnings_beat carries no tier-2 penalty, but consensus upside is only ~6% after a +36% run since Aug — it no longer clears the 20% gate. A hold, not a fresh entry.
